subject.title: feat(slack): allow configurable App Home views

question: Should file-backed Slack App Home content be process-stable configuration loaded through the Slack account lifecycle, or a supported live-edit surface reread on every Home event?
rationale: The publish fallback is mechanically repairable, but the no-restart file behavior intentionally conflicts with the repository's process-stable configuration and runtime hot-path guidance, so its permanent lifecycle requires owner intent.

options.title: Load through lifecycle
options.body: Resolve, size-bound, parse, and validate the file at account startup or explicit reload, leaving Home events filesystem-free.

options.title: Support live rereads
options.body: Retain event-time loading only with explicit ownership, a file-size bound, defined failure semantics, and operational proof.

recommendation.title: Load through lifecycle
recommendation.body: Resolve, size-bound, parse, and validate the file at account startup or explicit reload, leaving Home events filesystem-free.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent introduced and merged the current Slack App Home event and safe-rendering contract.
